messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: p99 latency alert for dedicated-pool://eu-west-2 exceeded 15s (SLO breach). Automated rollback disabled. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/1714306789

Alyssa (oncall): seeing it too. p95 trending up ~1.6s -> 3s, p99 spiking past 15s. Checking autoscaler and pool health.

Diego: queue depth reported 2.4k at peak on the tail router. Metrics snapshot:
```
queue.depth{pool="eu-west-2"} 2400
inflight.requests 780
autoscaler.pending_warmups 12
warmup.failures 9
```
Looks like warmup tasks are timing out during a rapid burst.

Maria: logs from a warmup job: 
```
[2026-03-15T15:06:12Z] warmup: starting model init on node i-0b12
[2026-03-15T15:06:45Z] warmup: kv-cache load success
[2026-03-15T15:07:01Z] warmup: cuda init timeout after 20s
[2026-03-15T15:07:02Z] warmup: reporting failure -> will retry
```
We've got multiple nodes hitting cuda init timeouts; possibly driver contention after burst.

Sam (sre): confirm autoscaler made scale decisions but pool readiness lagging. Autoscaler timeline: scale decision @15:04 (requested +6 nodes), cloud started instances 15:05-15:07, kube nodes joined 15:08-15:11, but warmup completed gradually 15:12-15:20. Meanwhile traffic spiked 15:03-15:10 so the warmup window missed the peak.

Alyssa (oncall): immediate mitigation ideas: 1) divert new requests to fallback model variant (lower GPU memory, already hot) 2) increase blacklist backoff for hotshot clients to reduce requeues 3) force-evacuate a subset of heavy jobs to Dedicated-hotshot pool. Thoughts?

Diego: on (1) — we can route by policy, but need to ensure compatibility. Using model-quantized-v2 as fallback might change quality for some customers. Can we apply at gateway for only non-enterprise tokens?

Maria: on (3) — heavy jobs are mostly long-context streaming, which are starving the pool. If we move long streams to the hotshot pool we reduce queue depth for short requests. Need to update routing rule and warm up 2 hotshot nodes first.

CS-Robot: Customer impact: 4 paying customers reported visible UX lag (chat streaming stalls). Estimated affected requests ~0.6% of total traffic during window, but for those customers p99 observed >20s. CS has opened tickets: TKT-3819, TKT-3822.

Sam (sre): doing an emergency scale override now (manual API): 
```
POST /internal/autoscale/override
{ "pool": "eu-west-2", "target": 18, "reason": "warmup lag during burst" }
```
This will create additional nodes and prioritize warmup threads. I'll watch readiness.

Alyssa (oncall): I pushed a temporary routing policy to divert non-enterprise tokens to model-quantized-v2 and enabled prefix caching for repeated short completions. Applied at API gateway (rule id gw-evac-15).

Diego: started draining long streams from dedicated-pool to hotshot-pool for new requests. Note: existing in-flight streams remain; we can't migrate those. Adding a circuit-breaker to avoid queue amplification: `max-queued-per-customer: 30`.

Maria: further note — observed driver OOM logs on two nodes during warmup, likely because warmup tries to load full 24GB weights in parallel with requests. Patching warmup to use streaming weight load (lower mem pressure) as a mitigation. Will deploy a quick patch to warmup job config.

Alyssa (oncall): timeline for mitigations: routing policy applied 15:18, scale-override requested 15:19, hotshot routing enabled 15:21, warmup patch rolled 15:30. Early signs of improvement: queue depth down from 2400 -> 430 by 15:35, p99 trending down to ~6s.

Sam (sre): confirming metrics now: 
```
p95 0.9s -> 1.2s (peak)
p99 15.6s -> 6.3s (post-mitigation)
queue.depth 2400 -> 430
warmup.failures 9 -> 2 (retries)
```
Not back to baseline but significantly improved. Continuing monitoring.

Diego: reminder: autoscaler policy review needed. The current warmup parallelism and cloud provisioning targets are too optimistic for bursty patterns. Opening PR to add burst-buffer reservations and staggered warmup.

Alyssa (oncall): customer impact summary for incident note: 4 customers affected, degraded streaming UX, p99 breaches lasted ~17 minutes (15:03-15:20). No errors/retries system-wide, mainly latency/polyphase stalls. CS has been notified and tickets are associated.

CS-Robot: CS update: customers TKT-3819 and TKT-3822 escalated to priority; customer calls scheduled 16:00 UTC.

Maria: capturing logs and snapshots for postmortem: warmup traces, node-init timings, driver logs, and gateway routing changes. Will attach to incident tracker INC-2026-045.

Sam (sre): handing off to next oncall (Diego) at 16:00 UTC. Diego — please keep monitoring until baseline recovered and start a follow-up with infra to tune autoscaler. I'll stay reachable for questions.

Diego: taking the handoff. I'll leave the override in place for 30m then start a gradual rollback once p99 < 2s for 20m. Opening a follow-up ticket: SVC-evac-2026 to review warmup strategy, autoscaler thresholds, and add a canary for cuda-init failures.

Alyssa (oncall): thanks team. Postmortem required, impact classification: Sev3 (customer-facing latency spike, partial degradation). I'll draft initial incident note and timeline.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 created and assigned to oncall: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2026-045

Diego: quick checklist before I sign off: 1) confirm override -> ok 2) verify gx-evac rule still active -> ok 3) ensure hotshot pool warmup health -> 2 nodes warming, expected ready 15:45. I'll keep thread updated.

(15:45 update) Diego: hotshot pool warmed, traffic split 80/20 in favor of normal pool (to avoid quality regression). p99 at 3.1s and decreasing. Leaving monitoring until 17:00 then rollback as described.

(17:01 update) Diego: rollback complete. Override removed, routing rules reverted, no further SLO breaches observed. Closing handoff. Follow-up tickets: SVC-evac-2026, PR#4528 (autoscaler burst-buffer), PM: schedule postmortem sync.
